entries.lead: EV-0213 — 6 November 1877 Clyde Street, Roath counterpart
entries.why: A Roath building plot leased to a builder, not the farm.

wiki_columns.heading: Record or assertion tested
wiki_columns.text: EV-0213 — 6 November 1877 Clyde Street, Roath counterpart

wiki_columns.heading: Disposition
wiki_columns.text: Ruled out as the farm lease. Photographs identify a house plot in Clyde Street, Roath; the lessee is John Williams, builder, of System Street, Roath; term 99 years from 29 September 1877, rent £2 12s 6d.

wiki_columns.heading: What it does and does not establish
wiki_columns.text: Explains why the exact date and 99-year term are a dangerous false friend. It does not identify the lessee as the Great House Farm tenant, prove a Llandough lease, or prove wrongdoing. A 99-year term from 1877 ends around 1976, not 1987.

wiki_columns.heading: Next step / retained route
wiki_columns.text: Keep the photos. Get the archive reference/bundle and Plan No. 15 so the catalogue identity can be authenticated; do not treat it as farm-title evidence.

entries.lead: DBDT/79/1 — 2 May 1877 Pembroke Terrace, Cardiff

wiki_columns.heading: Record or assertion tested
wiki_columns.text: DBDT/79/1 — 2 May 1877 Pembroke Terrace, Cardiff

wiki_columns.heading: Disposition
wiki_columns.text: Ruled out as a Llandough match. Physically examined; described in the archive correspondence as a Cardiff/Pembroke Terrace lease with no mention of Llandough, Great House Farm or Tŷ Mawr.

wiki_columns.heading: What it does and does not establish
wiki_columns.text: It is a real Bute–John Williams lease, but it concerns Cardiff property. The record does not show which Williams, if any, was related to the farm family.

wiki_columns.heading: Next step / retained route
wiki_columns.text: Keep as a negative control for name/date confusion. Use the archive’s corrected description, not older catalogue wording.

wiki_columns.text: Repository/app assertions of a 1667 “99-year” or “999-year” lease and of a 1983 title merger described as “proven” wrongdoing

wiki_columns.heading: Disposition
wiki_columns.text: Assertion text only; not evidence of its own truth.

wiki_columns.heading: What it does and does not establish
wiki_columns.text: The reviewed code contains incompatible lease terms and categorical legal conclusions without an identified instrument attached to those statements. Neither a 1877 Cardiff 99-year lease nor repeated app wording proves an earlier Tŷ Mawr lease or wrongdoing.

wiki_columns.heading: Next step / retained route
wiki_columns.text: Do not cite app copy as proof. Re-admit an assertion only when tied to an identified instrument, register entry, judgment passage or documented decision trail. Treat any charge of wrongdoing or concealment as untested until evidence establishes the necessary facts and state of knowledge.

entries.lead: Llandough Farm, the Rees family farm ( EV-0228 ; 1841 tithe, press 1865–1910), the 1940 WGR tenancy to David and Thomas Thomas ( EV-0233 ), and the dictated “R-W-S-S / Reese’s Farm” wording ( EV-0223 )

wiki_columns.text: Llandough Farm, the Rees family farm ( EV-0228 ; 1841 tithe, press 1865–1910), the 1940 WGR tenancy to David and Thomas Thomas ( EV-0233 ), and the dictated “R-W-S-S / Reese’s Farm” wording ( EV-0223 )

wiki_columns.heading: Disposition
wiki_columns.text: Separate farm. Directories list Thomas Rees at “Llandough” beside John Williams at “Great house” (1868, 1875, 1880). Llandough Farm is also the Roman villa site excavated in 1978–79 (GGAT HER).

wiki_columns.heading: What it does and does not establish
wiki_columns.text: Useful for telling the two farms apart. “R-W-S-S” is not on the photographed 1881 census page 2 ( EV-0224 ). Some press items call John Williams “of Llandough Farm” (1895, 1904), so the name alone does not settle which farm.

wiki_columns.heading: Next step / retained route
wiki_columns.text: Keep separate from the Great House chain unless a document joins them.

wiki_columns.heading: Record or assertion tested
wiki_columns.text: “Cardiff Urban District Council” as the water authority (per Branwen, voice testimony)

wiki_columns.heading: Disposition
wiki_columns.text: Name correction. No Cardiff UDC existed: Cardiff was a county borough. Llandough was in Penarth Urban District ( SC-22 ); the public water undertaker was Cardiff Corporation.

wiki_columns.heading: What it does and does not establish
wiki_columns.text: Either Penarth UDC or Cardiff Corporation could be the council remembered. The 1958 report blames Western Ground Rents, not a council.

wiki_columns.heading: Next step / retained route

entries.lead: “Mr. David Thomas, of Great House Farm, Llandough” (90th birthday, 1910), the 1907 “STRAYED” advert and the Glamorgan Hunt kennels farm
entries.source: 1871 census RG10/5417; Slater's 1880; Glamorgan Gazette 14 Oct 1910 p.8; Cardiff Times 23 Apr 1910 p.10
entries.why: The census puts David Thomas at the Cowbridge Great House; our farm was the Williamses'.
record: Glamorgan Gazette, 14 Oct 1910, p.8, under the paper's “COWBRIDGE.” heading: “Mr. David Thomas, of Great House Farm, Llandough, has just celebrated his 90th birthday.”

1871 census, RG10/5417 (Bridgend registration district, enumeration district 6, Llandough juxta Cowbridge), “Great House”: THOMAS David, Head, 50, “Farmer 140a Emp 4 Men&1 Boy”, born St Hilary. That places his birth about 1821, so he turned 90 in 1910 (transcription on FreeCEN).

Same census, our farm: RG10/5368 (Cardiff registration district, enumeration district 35, Llandough juxta Penarth), “Great House Farm”: WILLIAMS John, Head, 43, “Farmer 110 Acres, Emp 2 Men” (transcription on FreeCEN).
Slater's Directory 1880, Cowbridge section, Farmers: “IN LLANDOUGH PARISH. Morris Thomas, Llandough / Thomas David, Great House”.

Cardiff Times, 23 Apr 1910, p.10, Glamorgan puppy show: “luncheon subsequently at Mr Thomas's, Great House Farm, Llandough” (the Glamorgan Hunt kennels farm; Mr Arthur Spencer there in the Glamorgan Gazette, 3 May 1907).

Glamorgan Gazette, 27 Sep 1907 (also 4 and 11 Oct 1907): “STRAYED, to Great House Farm, Llandough … J. Thomas, Llandough” (read from search snippets only; the date is not yet confirmed from the page).
entries.establishes: Two farms called Great House stood in two parishes called Llandough. The deciding record is the 1871 census, which places David Thomas at Llandough juxta Cowbridge and John Williams at Llandough juxta Penarth. The 1910 birthday note, the 1907 advert and the hunt reports belong to the Cowbridge farm. They say nothing about Tŷ Mawr.
entries.next: None for the identity question. A 1911 census copy (RG14, Llandough-juxta-Cowbridge) would add the last household, but it is not needed to decide.

sources.text: Glamorgan Gazette 14 Oct 1910 p.8; 3 May 1907; 27 Sep, 4 Oct, 11 Oct 1907 (snippets)

entries.lead: Llandough Farm (the Corbett / Thomas holding), kept apart from Great House / Tŷ Mawr in the 25 Oct name search
entries.why: A separate farmstead: 166 acres in NLW D 219 against 107 acres for Cydfin / Tŷ Mawr.
record: The National Library of Wales catalogue keeps Llandough Farm (166 acres) apart from the 107-acre Cydfin / Tŷ Mawr lease group (NLW D 219).
The 1940 Western Ground Rents tenancy to David and Thomas Thomas (EV-0233) concerns Llandough Farm.

The 25 Oct 2026 search of every name the farm has gone by (Great House Farm, Great House, Tŷ Mawr / Ty Mawr / Tymawr, Cedfin or Ty Mawr Farm / Cydfin / Cedwyn, Llandough Home Farm) treated Llandough Farm as a distinct holding, not an alias.
entries.establishes: A positive identity correction: the two holdings are separate in the catalogue. The 166-acre figure and the Thomas tenancy cannot be carried over to Tŷ Mawr because both lie in the same parish.
entries.next: Examine the individual D 219 instruments and plans for exact boundaries.

entries.lead: Marquess of Bute v Seymour; Marquess of Bute v White; Barry Railway Co v Seymour; Barry Railway Co v White (Llandough right of way, 1905)
entries.place: Fields between the Cardiff–Sully road and Eastbrook (Green Seys / Cornerswell side), Llandough
entries.source: Evening Express 20, 28, 29, 31 Mar 1905; Western Mail 21, 23 Mar 1905
entries.why: Bute land on the Cornerswell side of the parish; no Williams and no Great House appears in any report.
record: The court's view: “Mr. Justice Lawrence, sitting in the Nisi Prius Court, Cardiff, formally entered judgment for plaintiffs in the Llandough right of way dispute case, and granted an injunction in the terms asked for—restraining trespassing on the land of the Barry Railway Company and also of the Marquess of Bute, with costs.” (Evening Express, 29 Mar 1905, p.3). The special jury's verdict for the plaintiffs came on 28 Mar 1905 (Glamorgan Assizes, before Lawrence J).

The action: “they each sued each of the two defendants … for damage for trespass on June 4, 1904. The defence was that the defendants were legitimately using a public path across fields at Llandough, the property of the Marques of Bute, and across the Barry Company's line, and leading from the Cardiff and Sully road to Eastbrook.” (Evening Express, 20 Mar 1905, p.3).
Counsel for Bute (a submission, not a finding): “Between the years 1848 and 1893 there was no person who could dedicate, because the estate was in strict settlement” (Evening Express, 28 Mar 1905).

Costs “including the expense of the assize action and the previous proceedings in London” were about £2,000; the defendants' share, about £500, was raised by public subscription (Evening Express, 31 Mar 1905, p.3).
The land named: the Green Seys (“Greensays”) fields, Cornerswell Farm, Westhouse, the One Acre Field (“Erw Heol Goch”) and a field of Colonel Homfray's.
entries.establishes: The same parish and the same landlord, Bute, but different land towards Dinas Powis. About twenty reports were read; none names Great House, Tŷ Mawr or the Williamses. Bute acting as owner of Llandough land in 1904–05 fits the Williamses being Bute's tenants.
entries.next: Only if family papers mention a path or trespass case: the Bute estate's own file (solicitor J. S. Corbett) in the Bute papers at Glamorgan Archives.

sources.text: Evening Express 20 Mar 1905 p.3; 28 Mar 1905; 29 Mar 1905 p.3; 31 Mar 1905 p.3 (Welsh Newspapers Online)
Western Mail 21 Mar 1905 p.5; 23 Mar 1905 p.7 (British Newspaper Archive index)

entries.lead: Poaching on Great House Farm, Llandough, prosecuted for the Bute Estate (Barry police court, Jan 1908)
entries.source: Evening Express 11 Jan 1908; Barry Dock News 17 Jan 1908
entries.why: Our farm, but a game prosecution: nothing in it bears on title or tenure.
record: The court's view: a Saltmead man “pleaded guilty … to poaching on Great House Farm, Llandough”; the underkeeper was John David; the sentence was two months (Evening Express, 11 Jan 1908).
“Mr L. Harris, solicitor, prosecuted on behalf of the Bute Estate” (Barry Dock News, 17 Jan 1908; read from a search snippet).
entries.establishes: It places the farm's name in a 1908 court report and shows the Bute Estate prosecuting game offences there. It does not show who held the freehold or on what terms the Williamses farmed.

entries.lead: “John Williams, Great House Farm, Llandough, was also fined £1” for travelling without a fare (Barry magistrates, Mar 1903)
entries.source: Barry Dock News 6 Mar 1903; Barry Herald 6 Mar 1903
entries.why: Our farm's name in a railway-fare case: no bearing on title or tenure.
record: The court's view: “John Williams, Great House Farm, Llandough, was also fined £1 for travelling between Grangetown and Cogan on the Barry Railway on the 12th ultimo, without having previously paid his fare.” (Barry Dock News, 6 Mar 1903). The Barry Herald of the same date gives “John Williams, jun.”
entries.establishes: It places a John Williams at Great House Farm in 1903, on the Penarth side (Grangetown to Cogan). That is all.
entries.next: None. Kept as a dated occupancy reference.

sources.text: Barry Dock News 6 Mar 1903 (Welsh Newspapers Online)

entries.lead: “John Williams, farmer, Llandough, was fined 20s.” (Penarth police court, Oct 1904)
entries.why: A licensing fine; which John Williams of Llandough is not settled, and it has no bearing on title.
record: The court's view: “John Williams, farmer, Llandough, was fined 20s. … for falsely representing himself to be a bona-fide traveller” (Evening Express, 12 Oct 1904, p.3; read from a search snippet).
entries.establishes: Nothing about the farm. Several Williamses farmed in Llandough parish, so the name alone does not identify the holding.

entries.lead: Whyte & Co. Ltd v Cardiff Corporation (Western Sewer contract arbitration, 1910–1912)
entries.place: Western District outfall sewer (Cardiff to Lavernock, through Llandough)
entries.source: Evening Express 11 Jun 1906, 14 Jul 1910; Western Mail 7 Mar, 24 Oct 1912; Dublin Builder 25 May 1912
entries.why: A contractor's money dispute with Cardiff Corporation, not a title or tenant case; it names no farm.
record: The arbitrator's view: Mr H. Percy Boulnois, M.Inst.C.E., “has given his award in the case of Whyte & Co., Ltd., v. Cardiff Corporation, in respect of a dispute which arose between the parties after the completion of the western [outfall sewer]” (Dublin Builder, 25 May 1912, p.28; snippet). The hearing ended at the Westminster Palace Hotel, London (Western Mail, 7 Mar 1912, p.5; snippet). The amount of the award has not been read (paywalled); the South Wales Weekly Argus of 11 May 1912 headed it “CARDIFF'S SURPRISE. Summary of the Award”.
The contract: Whyte & Co. of Belfast took Contract No. 6, Western Sewer, at £70,368 5s 4d (Evening Express, 11 Jun 1906).

The dispute: a final account of £123,452 3s 10d, “the difference of £53,083 16s. 6d. really represented extras”; the town clerk was asked “to advise the committee upon the legal questions involved” (Evening Express, 14 Jul 1910).
Afterwards a council row: Western Mail 24 Oct 1912 p.6; Western Mail 15 Jan 1913; South Wales Daily News 19 Feb 1913 p.6, “Cardiff Western Sewer. ‘NOTHING TO HIDE’” (snippets).
entries.establishes: The only dispute found that arose from the works the 23 Feb 1905 Bute conveyance to Cardiff served (EV-0013). It is a contract arbitration, not a court judgment, and nothing read shows it went on to the High Court. Whether Contract No. 6 was the Llandough section is not known.
entries.next: A paid reading of the 1912 award reports, or Cardiff borough Public Works Committee minutes 1910–13 at Glamorgan Archives.

sources.text: Evening Express 11 Jun 1906; 14 Jul 1910 (Welsh Newspapers Online)
Western Mail 7 Mar 1912 p.5; 24 Oct 1912 p.6; 15 Jan 1913 (snippets)
South Wales Weekly Argus 11 May 1912 p.8 (snippet)
South Wales Daily News 19 Feb 1913 p.6 (snippet)

entries.lead: Cardiff Corporation's injunction against Llandaff & Dinas Powis Rural District Council over Ely effluent (Local Government Board inquiry, 1904)
entries.place: River Ely and Cardiff's western sewer
entries.source: Evening Express 15 Jun 1904; Weekly Mail 18 Jun 1904
entries.why: A dispute between two councils about waste draining into the sewer; it does not concern the farm or the 1905 grant.
record: Cardiff Corporation sought an injunction against Llandaff & Dinas Powis RDC over Ely effluent draining into Cardiff's western sewer; the matter came before a Local Government Board inquiry (Evening Express, 15 Jun 1904; Weekly Mail, 18 Jun 1904). No outcome was read.
entries.establishes: Background to the western sewer scheme only. Both parties are public bodies.

entries.lead: “THE LLANDOUGH HOSPITAL. Legal Proceedings Possible” (Western Mail, 4 Oct 1934)
entries.source: Western Mail 4 Oct 1934 p.9 (snippet); Western Mail 2 Jul 1928
entries.why: A building contractor's final account against Cardiff Corporation at the hospital, not the farm.
record: Western Mail, 4 Oct 1934, p.9: “THE LLANDOUGH HOSPITAL. Legal Proceedings Possible”, about a contractor's final account against Cardiff Corporation (search snippet). Llandough Hospital was a Cardiff Corporation project (Western Mail, 2 Jul 1928).
entries.establishes: A Cardiff Corporation dispute at Llandough, separate from the 1905 conveyance and from the farm. No outcome was read.
entries.next: None unless the hospital land is shown to touch the farm.

entries.lead: The 1904 “one piece of land” arbitration flagged before the sewer easements (it apparently never happened)
entries.place: The Bute land on the western sewer line
entries.source: Weekly Mail 11 Jun 1904; Evening Express 9 Jun 1904; Cardiff Times 4 May 1907
entries.why: Never held: the corporation settled with the landowners without arbitration.
record: Weekly Mail, 11 Jun 1904: negotiations had been concluded with Sir W. T. Lewis “concerning easements over 2½ miles of land forming part of the Bute Estate … In respect of one piece of land arbitration proceedings will, probably, be unavoidable.” The landowner is not named.

Cardiff Times, 4 May 1907: Alderman Mildon said the corporation “had taken time to arrange matters with the landowners — a rather difficult matter — and had succeeded in doing that without going to arbitration”.
entries.establishes: A threatened arbitration that the record shows was avoided. It identifies no farm.

sources.text: Weekly Mail 11 Jun 1904; Evening Express 9 Jun 1904 (Welsh Newspapers Online)

entries.lead: “Cardiff City Corporation” as grantee of the 23 Feb 1905 Bute conveyance (Land Registry wording)
entries.place: Woodland on the north-east side of Leckwith Road, Llandough
entries.why: A name slip: Cardiff became a city only in Oct 1905, so the grantee was then the County Borough.
record: HM Land Registry, title WA735527, charges register entry 1: the land tinted pink is subject to the rights in “a Conveyance dated 23 February 1905 made between (1) John Marquis of Bute and Earl of Dumfries and (2) Cardiff City Corporation … Copy filed under WA231076.”
Cardiff received city status in October 1905.
entries.establishes: The register's wording is the registry's own paraphrase. It is not evidence of anything about the deed, which grants rights over a strip, not a transfer.
entries.next: An official copy of the deed and plan filed under WA231076 would show the strip and its purpose.

entries.lead: Re Nisbet and Potts' Contract [1906] 1 Ch 386 (Court of Appeal) — a precedent, not a farm case
entries.why: A reported precedent on adverse possession and covenants; it is not about Llandough land.
record: The court's view: acquiring title by adverse possession bars only the paper owner's claim; restrictive covenants that already bound the land still bind it, and the person in possession (Re Nisbet and Potts' Contract [1906] 1 Ch 386, CA). Related: Fairweather v St Marylebone Property Co Ltd [1963] AC 510.
entries.establishes: A rule of law, listed here because it surfaced in the day's search. Whether any pre-1955 burden on the land (for example the rights in the 1905 conveyance, EV-0013) bears on the 1987 case is a separate legal question, not settled here.
entries.next: List the known burdens in pre-1955 instruments and who could enforce them.

sources.text: Re Nisbet and Potts' Contract [1906] 1 Ch 386 (CA)
Fairweather v St Marylebone Property Co Ltd [1963] AC 510

entries.lead: “R. Hopkin, Great House, Llangadock” (prize list, 1906)
entries.why: A Great House in Carmarthenshire, not Llandough.
record: Evening Express, 26 Jun 1906, p.4 (a published list of names and addresses): “R. Hopkin, Great House. Llangadock.”
entries.establishes: Another farm called Great House. It shows how often the name occurs in the press.

sources.text: Evening Express 26 Jun 1906 p.4 (Welsh Newspapers Online)

entries.lead: “A. M. Thomas, Great House, Llanmaes” (show prize list, 1910)
entries.why: A Great House at Llanmaes, a third Glamorgan farm of the name.
record: Glamorgan Gazette, 12 Aug 1910, p.5, show prize list: “A. M. Thomas, Great House, Llanmaes.”
entries.establishes: A third Glamorgan Great House with a Thomas family. A Thomas “of Great House” in Vale press is not, by name alone, connected with Llandough.
entries.next: Check the parish before citing any “Great House” item.

sources.text: Glamorgan Gazette 12 Aug 1910 p.5 (Welsh Newspapers Online)

entries.lead: The “1924 Stewart survey” line “Late Thos. Williams now John Gedrick Tent.” — it is the 1824 Bute survey
entries.place: Cedfin or Ty Mawr Farm, Llandough-juxta-Penarth
entries.why: A dating slip: the record is ours, but it belongs to 1824.
record: The Stewart survey of the Bute estate, DB/E/1 plan 19 and reference table (1824), “Cedfin or Ty Mawr Farm”: “Late Thos. Williams now John Gedrick Tent.” (EV-0211).
A working note had dated the line 1924. No 1924 survey with this line is on file. The 15 May 1924 Bute–Corbett drain agreement (EV-0015) is a drain agreement and plan with no tenant line.
entries.establishes: The line is a record of our farm, from 1824, and names a late Thomas Williams in the Cedfin or Ty Mawr entry. The present transcription (139a 3r 8p; the name “John Gedrick”) remains provisional, as the wiki records.
entries.next: Use the 1824 date in every citation.

entries.lead: Proposed floor plan of another property, outside the Tŷ Mawr scope; parked for later inspection
entries.source: Architectural drawing image, received 27 October 2026 (no title block, site, author or date)
entries.why: Another property, outside the Tŷ Mawr scope; parked for later inspection.
record: A modern architectural drawing in millimetres headed “Proposed Ground Floor” and “Proposed First Floor”: on the ground floor a garage, office, kitchen, breakfast and dining rooms, lounge, formal garden, reflection pool, lawn, dorm, changing room, sauna and shower, plant room and studio; on the first floor a guest lounge and kitchen, guest bedrooms, bathroom, further bedrooms and a master bedroom with balcony.
No title block, site name, author or date appears on the drawing.
entries.establishes: Nothing about Tŷ Mawr / Great House Farm. The drawing is of another property and is kept here, out of the Wales evidence pages, for later inspection.
entries.next: Identify the property and the drawing’s source when convenient. No request is needed.
